docs.text: Zul’Akari Clans ¶ The Zul’Akari Clans are a confederation of jungle, marsh, and lake-dwelling peoples in the north-west of Arkhaven . They are difficult to conquer due to the density of their terrain, the danger of local wildlife and monsters, and the defensive knowledge of the clans who live there. Government ¶ Zul’Akari is governed by a council of elders representing the largest and most influential peoples within the region. These elders act as clan leaders and are advised by shamans, oracles, and other spiritual figures. Leadership is not fully centralised. The balance of power between the clans can shift depending on population, military strength, religious influence, and alliances between groups. Dominant Peoples ¶ The main peoples of Zul’Akari include: Tabaxi Batiri goblins Yuan-ti Purebloods Salamanders Lizardfolk Other minor groups, beasts, and rumoured monster-kin are believed to exist deeper within the jungles and marshes. Region and Biome ¶ Zul’Akari lies in the north-western reaches of Arkhaven. Its landscape is made up of dense jungle, wetlands, marshes, rivers, and access to a massive freshwater lake. The environment is humid, dangerous, and difficult for outsiders to navigate or occupy. Culture ¶ Zul’Akari culture is clan-based, territorial, and strongly tied to the land. Each people maintains its own customs, traditions, and social structures, though the clans will cooperate when facing external threats. Ancient ruins, dungeons, and lost sites are usually treated as sacred places rather than abandoned structures. Outsiders who attempt to loot them are likely to be treated as enemies. The clans also trade with the Free Peoples of Kharad in the Kharad Wildlands, particularly with goliath rulers and Loxodon communities. Religion and Magic ¶ Religion is important throughout Zul’Akari, but it varies between peoples. Different clans worship gods, spirits, ancestors, or powers associated with their own traditions. Shamans and oracles play a major role in advising leaders, interpreting omens, and maintaining spiritual authority. Magic is used by those races and individuals capable of it. The region’s ancient ruins are believed to contain powerful artifacts, forgotten spells, and other dangerous magical remnants. Tensions ¶ There are ongoing tensions between the ruling clans, especially as each group competes for influence within the council. Despite this, external threats usually force cooperation. The main outside pressures come from the Haskarn Freeholds, who are human expansionists, and the Eldermarch Court, whose northern jungle-themed elves have their own interests in the region.

docs.text: Arkhaven Regions ¶ Arkhaven is divided into several major geographic regions. These regions are not political entities, but broad environmental zones that shape climate, trade, settlement patterns, warfare, and culture. Many states occupy portions of multiple regions, while some regions contain several competing powers. Overview ¶ The continent is broadly divided into eight major regions: Region Characteristics Veylrain Expanse Tropical rainforests, wetlands, river deltas, lakes, and coastal jungles The Thornbelt Dry plains, scrublands, badlands, and frontier wilderness The Crimson Chain The fractured waterways and cliffs of the Godscar The Floodlands Marshes, lakes, floodplains, and river networks Arkenfall Northern forests, lakes, and eastern coastal frontiers Windmere Basin Fertile lowlands, river valleys, and southern agricultural heartlands Veridian March Temperate forests, rolling hills, and mixed woodland realms The Silent Weald Ancient forests, forgotten ruins, and lands touched by the Green Silence States within Arkhaven ¶ Many states occupy portions of multiple regions, while some regions contain several competing powers. Veylrain Expanse ¶ The Veylrain Expanse dominates the northern coastline of Arkhaven and contains some of the continent's oldest and most dangerous rainforests. Dense jungle stretches from the western coast to the eastern sea, broken only by rivers, wetlands, lakes, and scattered highlands. Heavy rainfall throughout much of the year creates a humid environment where vegetation rapidly consumes abandoned structures and forgotten roads. The Expanse is home to several powerful tribal societies, including the Zul’Akari Clans , Myruun Clans , Veylrath Clans , and Jhakur Clans . Ancient ruins are common throughout the region. Many remain unexplored, while others are protected by local peoples who regard them as sacred sites rather than sources of treasure. The Thornbelt ¶ The Thornbelt occupies much of north-central Arkhaven. It is a broad region of dry grassland, scrubland, rocky plains, seasonal rivers, and scattered hills. Conditions become increasingly harsh toward the interior, where water and fertile ground become valuable strategic resources. The Thornbelt serves as a natural buffer between the jungle societies of the north and the more settled states further south. Most of the region is occupied by the Kharad Wildlands , though portions of the Haskarn Freeholds , The Eldermarch Court , and neighbouring frontier territories extend into its edges. Trade routes crossing the Thornbelt are vital to communication between eastern and western Arkhaven. The Crimson Chain ¶ The Crimson Chain is the most strategically important region on the continent. Formed by the navigable waterways and steep cliffs of The Godscar , it divides much of Arkhaven while simultaneously providing one of its most important transportation corridors. Large lakes, deep river channels, fortified crossings, cliff roads, and narrow passages dominate the landscape. The region takes its name from the chain-like sequence of waterways extending from north to south through the continent. The Vermillion Crown controls many of the major crossings and passage routes, while The Leridian Concord and Court of Thalóriel maintain strong interests in the region. The Crimson Chain also contains the greatest concentrations of known veinstone deposits. Most exposed veins have been heavily worked over many centuries. Remaining deposits often appear as faint red crystalline seams with occasional flecks of gold visible within fractured cliff faces. The Floodlands ¶ The Floodlands occupy the north-eastern interior of Arkhaven. Unlike the dense jungles of the Veylrain Expanse, the Floodlands are characterised by vast marsh systems, shallow lakes, seasonal floodplains, and countless interconnected waterways. Travel is often dictated by water levels rather than roads. The region is dominated by The Skeldic Concord , although neighbouring powers maintain influence around its borders. Fishing, river trade, monster hunting, and wetland agriculture are important aspects of life throughout the region. Arkenfall ¶ Arkenfall forms the eastern frontier of northern Arkhaven. Its landscape consists of mixed forests, rugged coastlines, lakes, river valleys, and isolated uplands. While less densely forested than the Veylrain Expanse, it remains heavily wooded and relatively difficult to traverse. The region contains much of the territory of the Republic of Havenor and the eastern reaches of the Jhakur Clans . Historically, Arkenfall marked the frontier between expanding human settlement and the older peoples of the northern wilderness. Windmere Basin ¶ The Windmere Basin occupies much of south-eastern Arkhaven. Fed by rivers descending from both the Anvilspine Range and the mountains of the Dornhal Empire , it is one of the most fertile regions on the continent. The basin contains rich farmland, vineyards, orchards, river valleys, market towns, and major trade roads. The Windmere Assembly occupies much of the southern basin, while the Dornhal Empire and The Throne of Khuldovar control the surrounding highlands and mountain systems. Its wealth derives from agricultural abundance, trade, and access to both inland and coastal routes. Veridian March ¶ The Veridian March stretches across much of western and central Arkhaven. The region consists primarily of temperate forests, rolling hills, grasslands, rivers, and settled woodland. Compared to the harsher northern regions, the Veridian March supports dense populations and numerous long-established states. The region includes portions of the The Verdant Confederacy , Houses of Bârathanaear , The Eldermarch Court , Tirith I Daur , and neighbouring territories. Many of the oldest roads outside the Godscar pass through the Veridian March, making it one of the most interconnected regions on the continent. The Silent Weald ¶ The Silent Weald occupies much of south-western Arkhaven and is closely associated with the historical event known as The Green Silence . The region is dominated by ancient forests, overgrown ruins, abandoned roads, hidden settlements, forgotten sacred sites, and stretches of woodland that appear untouched by conventional history. Many locations within the Weald appear to have been altered by the Green Silence. Roads vanish beneath centuries of growth. Entire settlements survive only in fragmented records. Different maps often disagree on the locations of old towns, shrines, and trade routes. The region contains large portions of The Martarië Crown , Court of Thalóriel , and Tirith I Daur . To this day, the Silent Weald remains one of the most mysterious regions in Arkhaven. It contains no single ruin, battlefield, or monument that can definitively explain the Green Silence. Instead, evidence is scattered throughout the forests themselves, hidden beneath roots, beneath moss-covered stone, and within contradictory records preserved by different cultures. The Green Silence is believed to have affected both the physical landscape and the historical record. Roads became impassable. Settlements disappeared beneath forest growth. Shrines became inaccessible. Written records were lost, restricted, damaged, or removed. Regional travel became less predictable, and later generations inherited conflicting accounts of places that once seemed well known. For many scholars, the Silent Weald remains one of the greatest unanswered mysteries in the history of Lazuril.

docs.text: The history of Lazuril is commonly divided into broad historical ages used by scholars, Scriptors, churches, archive houses, and historians. Exact dates remain heavily disputed. Different cultures use different historical systems, and some regions reject standardised chronology entirely. The major ages are therefore best understood as broad historical frameworks rather than universally agreed periods. Modern chronology throughout much of Arkhaven is measured from the beginning of The Green Silence , recognised as 1 GS. Age Before Memory ¶ The Age Before Memory refers to the earliest period of known history. Very little reliable information survives from this era. Most knowledge comes from: Fragmentary ruins Religious tradition Astronomical records Deep-earth discoveries Oral mythology Isolated archive fragments Several major civilisations are believed to have existed during this period, though little is known with certainty. Age of Fracture ¶ The Age of Fracture refers to the period surrounding The Godscar . The age is associated with: Continental upheaval Religious transformation Mass migration Political collapse Large-scale destruction Changes to geography and waterways The Godscar predates all currently documented peoples of Arkhaven. Modern cultures preserve interpretations and theories rather than direct knowledge of its true origin. Many churches treat this period as one of the defining moments in mortal history. Post-Godscar Era ¶ The Post-Godscar Era describes the long reconstruction period following the Age of Fracture. Several later kingdoms, churches, trade systems, and settlement patterns trace their origins to this period. The era also includes the establishment or expansion of several currently recognised peoples within Arkhaven. This includes early dwarven holds in the mountains, elven archive traditions in the south-western forests, tabaxi communities in the northern rainforests, and the later human arrival known as the Arkfall. Much surviving written history begins during the later stages of this era. Era of Silence ¶ The Era of Silence begins with the Green Silence in 1 GS. The period is characterised by: Lost settlements Broken roads Disrupted records Isolated populations Disappearing forest regions Historical uncertainty Large gaps in surviving history originate from this era. Age of False Saints ¶ The Age of False Saints refers to the period surrounding War of the False Saints . The conflict is generally believed to have occurred more than a century before the current era. The age was marked by: Religious conflict Doctrinal instability False miracles Forged relics Saint cults Political manipulation of religion Human-led churches and states were major accelerants of the crisis, although they were not the only participants. The age eventually led to the creation of The Scriptor Compact . Compact Era ¶ The Compact Era is the current historical age used by many major institutions in Arkhaven. The era is characterised by: Increased record standardisation Greater institutional cooperation Expansion of archive systems Growth of trade networks Wider use of Scriptors Continued political fragmentation The current historical period is generally recognised as being slightly more than five centuries after the beginning of the Green Silence. Despite greater stability, many unresolved tensions from earlier ages remain active.

docs.text: The calendar systems of Lazuril vary between cultures, kingdoms, churches, and historical traditions. Most modern systems used in Arkhaven now measure time using the beginning of The Green Silence as the primary historical reference point. Under this system, the first recorded year of the Green Silence is recognised as 1 GS . The current historical period is generally understood to be slightly more than twelve centuries after the beginning of the event. Overview ¶ Most major calendars are based upon: Solar cycles Lunar observation Seasonal change Astronomical events Religious observance Although regional systems still exist, the GS dating system is widely used by: Churches Archive Houses Scriptors Trade institutions Historians Major governments Seasons ¶ Most regions recognise four major seasons. Seasonal intensity varies significantly depending on geography and climate. Northern rainforests, desert regions, mountain territories, and glacial elevations often experience seasonal conditions very differently from the central grasslands. Religious Observances ¶ Many churches maintain holy days, fasts, pilgrimage periods, and commemorative festivals tied to: Solstices Equinoxes Historical events Saints Celestial alignments Agricultural cycles Religious calendars do not always align between institutions. Astronomy and Navigation ¶ Astronomical observation remains important for: Navigation Agriculture Religious ritual Maritime travel Seasonal prediction Historical record keeping Elven observatories and maritime powers maintain some of the most accurate astronomical records. Historical Usage ¶ The adoption of the GS system became increasingly widespread after the Age of False Saints and the expansion of institutional record keeping under the Scriptor Compact. Many historians considered the Green Silence a more stable historical reference point than earlier disputed events associated with the Godscar. Older records may therefore use different chronological systems. Current Status ¶ Although no single calendar system dominates all of Lazuril, the GS dating system is now the closest equivalent to a continental standard throughout much of Arkhaven. Regional variations remain common, especially in isolated territories and older religious traditions.

docs.text: Aasimar ¶ Aasimar are rare human-descended bloodlines on Arkhaven , marked by traces of celestial ancestry carried across the sea aboard the first Ark. Arkborne Nobility ¶ They did not arrive as a separate people or wandering outsiders. The first Aasimar families came among the early human nobility, priests, officers, and chosen settlers who helped establish the first human foothold on the continent. Because of their status, many Aasimar bloodlines were granted large plots of land in the new world. For generations, these families benefited from early claims, inherited estates, temple patronage, civic office, and the prestige of being linked to the Ark’s founding families. Modern Bloodlines ¶ In modern Arkhaven, Aasimar are most strongly associated with old human states such as the Republic of Havenor , where several respected families still claim celestial ancestry from the first arrivals. Their bloodlines are often treated with reverence, suspicion, or resentment depending on local history. Not all Aasimar are wealthy or noble today. Some families lost their lands, diluted their claims, or rejected the privileges of their ancestors. Even so, the old association remains: to many people of Arkhaven, Aasimar are living reminders of the Ark, the first human settlement, and the unequal rewards that followed.

docs.text: Dwarves are one of the major civilised peoples of Arkhaven . They are most strongly associated with the south-eastern mountain ranges of the continent, where their oldest kingdoms, deepest mines, and largest strongholds are located. Their principal homeland is The Throne of Khuldovar , centred on the great mountain-capital of Khuldovar. The Dornhal Empire is also dwarven, though culturally and politically distinct, having split from Khuldovar many centuries ago. Dwarven civilisation is shaped by stone, metal, pressure, heat, and depth. Their settlements are commonly built within mountains rather than upon them, and many dwarven societies measure wealth, prestige, and history through craftsmanship, engineering, oath-keeping, and the endurance of their halls. Large dwarven holds, mining enclaves, fortress-cities, tunnel stations, and trade halls exist throughout the mountain regions of Arkhaven. Smaller dwarven communities are also found near human cities, major construction projects, river routes, strategic passes, and mixed states such as the Windmere Assembly . Dwarves are widely respected as miners, masons, smiths, armourers, engineers, bridge-builders, and fortification experts. Human and mixed states often rely on dwarven skill for roads, walls, tunnels, weapons, locks, and stonework. Their societies are usually organised around clans, guilds, ancestral lineages, and sworn obligations. Political disputes between dwarven powers can be severe, but dwarven contracts are generally treated across Arkhaven as among the most reliable in the world. In modern Arkhaven, dwarves remain economically powerful beyond their population size. Their mountains provide metal, stone, engineering knowledge, military strength, and deep historical memory. To many dwarves, the deep earth is not only a source of wealth. It is history itself.

docs.text: Elves are one of the oldest surviving peoples of Arkhaven . Their civilisation predates most modern kingdoms, organised churches, and written human histories on the continent. They are most strongly associated with the south-western forests, especially the region now known as the Silent Weald after The Green Silence . Most major elven settlements, archives, academies, noble houses, and sacred groves remain concentrated in these forests. The main elven powers include The Martarië Crown , Tirith I Daur , Houses of Bârathanaear , The Eldermarch Court , and the Court of Thalóriel . Elves also hold influence in mixed states such as the Verdant Confederacy and the Windmere Assembly . Elven society places unusually high importance on continuity, memory, language, education, magical discipline, and the preservation of knowledge. This became even more important after the Green Silence, when large parts of older elven culture were swallowed by the forest and many records were lost. Because of this history, elves are diligent record keepers. Documents are copied, witnessed, translated, sealed, and stored in separate archives so that history cannot vanish in the same way again. This cultural habit is one of the main reasons elves became closely involved in the creation and operation of The Scriptor Compact . Elven magic is usually associated with illusion, divination, enchantment, warding, preservation, ritual practice, and memory. After the War of the False Saints , elven illusionists became controversial, but also valuable, because they were among the best suited to identifying false miracles and magical deception. In modern Arkhaven, elves remain one of the continent’s major political, scholarly, and religious influences. Their population is smaller than humanity’s, but their long lives, archives, magical education, and Scriptor institutions allow them to hold influence far beyond their numbers.

docs.text: Humans are the most widespread and politically dominant people on Arkhaven , but they are not considered native to the continent. Human histories describe their arrival by sea aboard a small fleet of arks, expeditionary ships, and survival vessels. These ships carried sailors, settlers, priests, soldiers, craftspeople, scholars, officers, nobles, and families from an older homeland beyond the horizon. The name Arkhaven is human in origin: to the earliest settlers, the continent was a haven reached by ark. The first human landing is most strongly associated with the Republic of Havenor , the oldest human-founded state on the continent. From these early coastal settlements, humans expanded inland over generations, founding farms, towns, churches, roads, ports, and fortified states. Today, humans dominate or strongly influence several major realms, including the Republic of Havenor, The Vermillion Crown , the Verdant Confederacy , and the Windmere Assembly . Human populations also exist in many mixed regions, frontier settlements, trade towns, religious centres, and conquered or contested territories. Human power in Arkhaven is based on adaptation, population growth, agriculture, settlement expansion, trade, religious organisation, military flexibility, and political ambition. There is no single human ruler. Human states compete with one another as often as they compete with neighbouring peoples. The human legacy is contested. Many humans see themselves as descendants of desperate survivors who crossed the sea and built a new home. Older peoples often remember the same process as colonisation, land seizure, displacement, treaty-breaking, forced conversion, and cultural absorption. Human-led churches and states were major accelerants of the War of the False Saints , partly because their institutions were younger, their records less stable, and their rulers eager for divine legitimacy. This history contributed directly to the later authority of The Scriptor Compact . In modern Arkhaven, humans control many of the continent’s largest cities, farmland regions, trade routes, ports, churches, and armies. Their central legacy remains one of survival becoming entitlement.

docs.text: Tabaxi ¶ Tabaxi are a feline humanoid people found primarily in the northern territories of Arkhaven , especially within the tropical rainforests, dense jungle, river basins, and coastal forest regions. Northern Clanlands ¶ They are most strongly associated with the clan-held lands of the north, including the Veylrath Clans , Jhakur Clans , Myruun Clans , and Zul’Akari Clans . These regions are not ruled as single centralised kingdoms, and many tabaxi communities remain organised around kin-groups, treetop settlements, river clans, shrine families, and travelling bands. Tabaxi culture is shaped by movement, curiosity, oral tradition, sign language, hunting, trade secrecy, and survival in difficult forest terrain. Many settlements are built high in the canopy, with hidden platforms, rope bridges, rain collectors, lookout perches, and concealed nursery spaces. Reputation and Survival ¶ Outsiders often know tabaxi as agile scouts, guides, traders, messengers, and storytellers. Their knowledge of northern forest routes is valuable, but rarely given away freely. A tabaxi guide may lead travellers through the jungle, but most will never reveal the full location of a clan home or canopy road. Tabaxi communities are cautious because they have a long history of defending themselves from predators, raiders, traffickers, and those who attempted to capture young tabaxi for sale. This has made secrecy a cultural necessity rather than simple suspicion. Some tabaxi live in port towns, trade cities, or mixed frontier settlements, but most remain culturally tied to the hidden communities of the northern forests. Their central concern is survival without captivity, trade without exposure, and freedom without surrendering the safety of their young.

docs.text: Lazuril is the known world upon which the continent of Arkhaven exists. The world is dominated by vast oceans, separated continental landmasses, deep climatic variation, ancient religious history, and long-lived civilisations whose records often contradict one another. The name "Lazuril" is commonly associated with the blue appearance of the world when viewed through astronomical instruments or described in older cosmological writings. Overview ¶ Lazuril contains multiple continents, major ocean systems, isolated island chains, polar regions, and large unexplored territories. Only portions of the world are well documented. Most surviving historical records originate from: Arkhaven Elven archive houses Dwarven engineering records Religious institutions Maritime trade powers Large sections of the world remain poorly mapped. Astronomy ¶ The study of astronomy is practiced by scholars, navigators, Scriptors, sailors, and religious observatories throughout Lazuril. Several major cultures maintain differing cosmological models regarding: The movement of celestial bodies The divine structure of the heavens The origins of the world The role of magic in the cosmos The relationship between the gods and the stars Astronomical observation is especially important for navigation and calendar keeping. Continents ¶ Arkhaven is currently the best documented continent in surviving records. Other continental landmasses are known to exist beyond the surrounding seas, though many remain politically or geographically distant from the affairs of Arkhaven. Some are known primarily through: Merchant records Sailor testimony Pilgrimage accounts Diplomatic reports Fragmentary maps Ancient archive references Oceans and Seas ¶ The oceans of Lazuril are major drivers of trade, migration, climate, and political influence. Long-distance travel remains dangerous due to: Storm systems Sea monsters Navigational uncertainty Piracy Uncharted waters Seasonal currents Despite this, maritime trade connects large parts of the known world. Historical Ages ¶ Most historians divide the history of Lazuril into broad historical ages. Exact dates remain disputed. Major eras commonly referenced include: The Age Before Memory The Age of Fracture The Post-Godscar Era The Era of Silence The Age of False Saints The Compact Era These classifications are used differently between cultures and institutions. Religion ¶ Religion is one of the defining forces of Lazuril. The gods are widely accepted as real entities capable of interacting with the mortal world through divine magic, prophecy, visions, omens, and miracles. At the same time, the history of Lazuril demonstrates that divine claims can be manipulated, misunderstood, or falsified. This tension heavily influences politics, scholarship, and law. Current Status ¶ Lazuril remains politically fragmented and historically incomplete. Ancient ruins, disputed records, forgotten roads, submerged structures, and lost civilisations continue to shape the modern world. Many scholars believe significant portions of Lazurilian history remain undiscovered, concealed, or deliberately restricted.
